summary: The appellant challenged the Karnataka High Court's order discharging the respondent from charges under Section 13(1)(e) read with Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, on grounds that the sanction to prosecute was illegal. The respondent, a former Executive Engineer, was accused of possessing assets disproportionate to known income. After investigation, sanction was granted by the State Government in 2010, leading to a chargesheet and framing of charges in 2014. The respondent had previously withdrawn his discharge application in 2014, but later filed successive discharge applications challenging the sanction's validity. The trial court dismissed the third application after 17 prosecution witnesses were examined. The High Court allowed a petition under Section 482 CrPC, discharging the respondent. The Supreme Court held that the High Court erred in interfering under Section 482 CrPC by revisiting the validity of sanction, which is barred under Section 19(3) and (4) of the PCA, 1988, absent failure of justice. The trial court’s findings on sanction could not be reversed in revision.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 13(1)(e) read with Section 13(2), Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Karnataka Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1957, Rule 10
final_judgment: The appeal is allowed, the impugned judgment of the High Court is set aside, and the proceedings before the Special Court are restored.
